reasoning: Mandatory answer-first experiment: the hook states the fact itself with a concrete claim and avoids the 'What X does' shapes. I chose the human body because body Reels get the most distribution (about 100 reach on sleep, cold water, voice, height and death zone). Blood vessel length is new, visual and easy to verify. Four short slides keep the Reel tight, and every slide carries a number in the highlight to make it hit harder. Music and palette rotate (mystery, palette 0). The CTA teases a daily fact to test follow conversion, and the caption adds a follow reason as the strategy asks.
topic: Length of blood vessels: 100,000 km, capillaries, circulation time, heart output
hook: Your blood vessels could circle Earth twice

slides.title: Longer than you think
slides.body: Laid end to end, an adult's blood vessels stretch about 100,000 km. Earth's equator is about 40,000 km.
slides.image_prompt: Glowing red branching vessel network wrapped around a small globe of Earth, dark background, cinematic lighting
slides.credit:
Courtesy of NIAID

Ryan Kissinger (Public domain) via wikimedia

slides.title: Mostly tiny capillaries
slides.body: Most of that length is capillaries, so narrow that red blood cells squeeze through in single file.
slides.image_prompt: Microscopic view of red blood cells lined up one by one inside a narrow translucent tube, soft red glow

slides.title: One lap per minute
slides.body: At rest, your blood makes a full trip around your body in about one minute.
slides.image_prompt: Stopwatch made of glass filled with flowing red liquid circling inside it, dark moody background

slides.title: A tireless pump
slides.body: Your heart pushes about 7,500 liters of blood through this network every single day.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical heart model beside dozens of large glass bottles of red liquid, dramatic side lighting

caption:
An adult's blood vessels add up to roughly 100,000 km. That is about two and a half times around Earth's equator, packed inside one body.

Most of that length is capillaries, which are thinner than a hair. Your heart still pushes around 7,500 liters of blood through them every day. Source: Cleveland Clinic, NIH NHLBI.

Follow for one body fact your brain won't believe, every day. Which number surprised you most: 100,000 km or 7,500 liters?
